where: Section 1, end of the paragraph on confinement
problem: The sentence "Both raise gain per unit volume and lower threshold current" is loose. Carrier confinement raises the gain per unit volume, because it packs carriers into a small active region. Optical confinement does not change the gain per unit volume; it raises the fraction of the optical mode that overlaps the active layer (the confinement factor Γ), which raises the modal gain Γg. A student can read this sentence as saying the index step also multiplies the material gain.
fix: Carrier confinement raises the gain per unit volume. Optical confinement raises the overlap of the mode with the active layer, that is, the confinement factor Γ, so the modal gain Γg rises. Both lower the threshold current.

problem: The term E₁h in "E_g + E₁e + E₁h" is never defined. The student has seen only the electron mass in the formula and may not know that the hole level uses the hole effective mass.
fix: The emitted photon energy is E_g + E₁e + E₁h, where E₁e is the first electron level, computed with the electron effective mass m*e, and E₁h is the first hole level, computed with the same formula using the hole effective mass m*h.
